rules: Docs navigation, family metadata, token inspection, and catalog browsing remain docs-shell concerns and must not be required inside the shared demo target.
The shared demo app may be launched or inspected from the docs shell, but its core screens must stand on their own without docs-only chrome.
The demo contract owns screen structure, state posture, and component usage; the docs shell owns catalog navigation, package metadata, and token-inspector utilities.

shellRegions.purpose: Top-level identity, navigation entry points, and global actions.
Primary screen switching inside the demo app without using docs navigation.
Screen-local filters, segmented controls, and state toggles.
Main task surface for the current demo screen.
Secondary detail, review, or supporting state surface.
Persistent shell status, summary, and mode visibility.
Command, picker, dialog, drawer, and other transient overlay surfaces.

screenContracts.title: Overview shell
interactionCheckpoints: shell hierarchy remains readable without docs metadata chrome
global actions and shell status remain reachable with keyboard-only traversal
status and remediation posture remain visible without collapsing into toast-only feedback
the primitive coverage deck keeps every public primitive directly reviewable without leaving the shared demo shell

screenContracts.title: Form and validation
interactionCheckpoints: field labels, help text, and validation posture remain attached to the same screen story
focus entry, error recovery, and action enablement remain explicit
notification or remediation surfaces remain part of the workflow instead of separate docs examples

screenContracts.title: Browse and table
interactionCheckpoints: filters, search, table selection, and no-results posture read as one coherent browse workflow
bulk actions and pagination stay attached to visible selection semantics
list or table mode switching remains part of the screen model rather than separate section demos

screenContracts.title: Detail and related data
interactionCheckpoints: headers, metadata, cards, and supporting content remain part of one believable detail workflow
value alignment and card hierarchy stay strong across themes and densities
detail navigation and supporting summaries are visible without docs-catalog framing

screenContracts.title: Picker and media
interactionCheckpoints: selection workflow, preview framing, and fallback posture remain one story instead of separate section samples
inline and overlay picker modes preserve the same visible workflow semantics
media fallback and unavailable-preview posture stay intentional rather than renderer-specific noise

screenContracts.title: Command and workspace
interactionCheckpoints: command discovery and workstation hierarchy remain part of the same shell target
modal command posture, panel tabs, and dock regions stay readable under side-by-side review
workspace status, persistence cues, and companion-panel state remain visible without docs-shell interference

parityChecklist: Each demo screen must preserve the same screen purpose and shell hierarchy in Svelte and GPUI.
Public component usage should be visible enough that the screen reads as built from the shared packages rather than from ad-hoc demo glue.
Every public primitive export must be directly reviewable somewhere inside the shared demo shell, even when multiple specimens are grouped on one coverage deck.
Theme, density, and control size remain first-class review dimensions for the same demo screens in both runtimes.
Focus entry, focus recovery, keyboard traversal, and state exposure must be reviewed at the screen level rather than only at isolated component level.
Any runtime-specific differences must be recorded through the intentional delta register instead of becoming implicit demo drift.
nonGoals: Do not treat the docs shell as the demo app contract.
Do not make Bits-specific or GPUI-specific mechanics part of the demo contract.
Do not require every exported component to become its own detached screen or specimen if that breaks the coherence of the target app.
